summary: Sonnet review of the Isaac-only parts of the new photoreal scenario renderer, each finding verified

result.title: Extra sim.render() subframes only accumulate if nothing resets path-tracing accumulation; pin /rtx/resetPtAccumOnAnimTimeChange and verify with a convergence probe
result.description: Answer to item 3. The keys and values at L139-147 are right, and the ordering is right: SimulationContext.__init__ runs _apply_render_settings_from_cfg(), which calls rep.settings.set_render_rtx_realtime(antialiasing='DLAA') and then 'WAR: Ensure /rtx/renderMode RaytracedLighting is correctly cased' (simulation_context.py:798-809). That forces real-time mode, and your later sim.set_setting('/rtx/rendermode','PathTracing') overrides it. Semantics per NVIDIA: spp = samples per pixel per frame; totalSpp = cap on accumulated samples, and 'When this count is reached the rendering stops until a scene or setting change is detected, restarting the rendering process.' Your per-video-frame protocol is therefore consistent: apply_state() changes the camera (Fabric write) and the link transforms, so accumulation restarts by design; sim.step's app.update renders spp=32; each of the 3 extra sim.render() calls adds 32 until totalSpp = spp*subframes = 128. Restarting every video frame is NOT a problem. The weak link is that the extra renders only add samples if the renderer sees no change between them. Isaac Sim's SimulationContext calls self._timeline.set_auto_update(True) (isaacsim.core.api simulation_context.py L132), so timeline time advances on every app.update, including the ones from Isaac Lab's render(), which only toggles /app/player/playSimulations (simulation_context.py:625-627). If /rtx/resetPtAccumOnAnimTimeChange is True on Kit 107, every extra render restarts accumulation, so you pay 4x render time for 32-spp images. I could not read the Kit 107 default (docs.omniverse.nvidia.com is blocked by the egress policy). NVIDIA's ov_sample dofbot sets it True to 'fix the PathTracing + Play producing line artifacts', which implies the default is not True, and other Isaac Sim path-tracing users pin it False. Treat it as unverified and pin it. Also: the Isaac Lab Camera annotator does receive the path-traced, denoised LdrColor of the last app.update. Replicator's Orchestrator is disabled and asyncRendering=false in apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit, so each app.update renders every render product and fills the annotators.
result.evidence: isaac-sim/IsaacSim source/standalone_examples/api/isaacsim.replicator.examples/motion_blur_pathtracing.py L170-174 (copy at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/ext_ev/motion_blur_pt.py): '# (int): Total number of samples for each rendered pixel, per frame.  settings.set("/rtx/pathtracing/spp", ...)  # (int): Maximum number of samples to accumulate per pixel. When this count is reached the rendering stops until a scene or setting change is detected, restarting the rendering process. Set to 0 to remove this limit.  settings.set("/rtx/pathtracing/totalSpp", ...)  settings.set("/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/enabled", 0)'. Same keys with /rtx/rendermode='PathTracing' are used in an Isaac Lab ManagerBasedEnv (TeleHuman/OASIS tasks/teleop/replayer.py: env.sim.set_setting('/rtx/rendermode','PathTracing'); set_setting('/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/enabled', True); set_setting('/rtx/pathtracing/totalSpp', 32)) and in Matterix RenderCfg(carb_settings={'/rtx/rendermode':'PathTracing','/rtx/pathtracing/spp':64,'/rtx/pathtracing/totalSpp':512,'/rtx/pathtracing/maxBounces':6}), so spp/totalSpp/maxBounces/optixDenoiser/enabled all exist in Isaac Lab 2.x / Isaac Sim 5.x. Isaac Sim SimulationContext.step(render=True) is a single self._app.update() (L729-740 of the deprecated isaacsim.core.api copy). Reset key evidence: KazWong/omniverse_sample dofbot_dataset.py '# turn this on to fix the PathTracing + Play (needed for overlap test) producing line artifacts: set_bool("/rtx/resetPtAccumOnAnimTimeChange", True)'; YCJ0815/3D-Diffusion-Policy replay_trajectories_isaacsim.py sets '/rtx/resetPtAccumOnAnimTimeChange': False next to optixDenoiser keys.

verdict.reason:
The finding does not establish a defect. Its own text says the Kit 107 default for /rtx/resetPtAccumOnAnimTimeChange is unverified. A grep of source/ apps/ scripts/ for resetPtAccum and clampSpp finds nothing, so the repo gives no evidence either way. The cited evidence points the other way. One sample sets the key True only to fix PathTracing-plus-Play line artifacts, which implies the default is not True. The other samples set it False explicitly.

The mechanism it fears is also weakly supported by the Isaac Lab source. Isaac Lab's render() (simulation_context.py around L615-632) sets /app/player/playSimulations to False around self._app.update(), so the extra sim.render() calls run with simulation play paused. The claim that the timeline advances on every extra render, and so resets accumulation, is asserted, not shown. My recollection, which I could not verify offline, is that the Omniverse RTX documentation lists this key with a default of False.

The per-frame camera and link pose change already restarts accumulation by design, as the finding concedes. The extra renders therefore add samples only while the scene is static between them, which is the intended protocol.

The 'clampSpp' suggestion is likewise speculative. At most this is an optional defensive pin plus an on-hardware convergence probe, not a verified bug. It is worth doing only if sample accumulation is actually suspect on the real machine. Pinning the key to False is harmless.

result.title: The try/except around sim.set_setting can never fire; a wrong or misspelled RTX key is silently created and ignored
result.description: SimulationContext.set_setting uses carb set_bool/set_int/set_float/set_string, and by its own docstring creates unknown keys instead of failing. So the except branch at L146-147 is dead code, and a key that does not exist in this Kit build (or a type that does not match) just becomes an inert setting while the render silently stays on defaults. All five keys you use are real (see the previous finding), but this is the exact failure mode for any future key change, for example on a Kit upgrade. Isaac Lab's own RenderCfg.carb_settings path validates ('does not map to a carb setting'), but it is not usable here for the reason given above (DLAA reset order).
result.evidence: source/isaaclab/isaaclab/sim/simulation_context.py:463-466: 'If the input setting name does not exist, it will be created. If it does exist, the value will be overwritten. Please make sure to use the correct setting name.'; validation only in the carb_settings branch at :794-795: 'if self.get_setting(key) is None: raise ValueError(f"... does not map to a carb setting.")'.
result.fix:
Replace the loop body at L144-147 with a registered-key check and a read-back:
    for key, value in (...):
        if sim.get_setting(key) is None:
            print(f'[scenario] WARNING: {key} is not a registered carb setting in this Kit build; RTX will ignore it', flush=True)
        sim.set_setting(key, value)
    print('[scenario] render settings:', {k: sim.get_setting(k) for k in ('/rtx/rendermode','/rtx/pathtracing/spp','/rtx/pathtracing/totalSpp','/rtx/pathtracing/maxBounces','/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/enabled')}, flush=True)
    assert sim.get_setting('/rtx/rendermode') == 'PathTracing'
For --renderer rtx, 'RealTimePathTracing' is also a valid /rtx/rendermode in Isaac Sim 5.x (OmniGibson sets it) if you want a faster, path-traced-quality real-time mode.

verdict.reason: The core claim holds. SimulationContext.set_setting (source/isaaclab/isaaclab/sim/simulation_context.py:460-485) has a docstring saying a missing setting name "will be created". It only calls carb set_bool/set_int/set_float/set_string, and raises ValueError only for an unsupported value type. The values here (bool, int, str) are all supported, and args_cli.spp is argparse type=int (render_scenario.py:39), so the except at L146-147 cannot realistically fire. A misspelled or unregistered /rtx key would silently become an inert carb setting. The only validation in Isaac Lab is the `get_setting(key) is None` check in the carb_settings branch (~L794-795), which this script does not use. Two parts of the proposed fix are weak. (1) `assert sim.get_setting('/rtx/rendermode') == 'PathTracing'` and the read-back print are vacuous: they read back the value just written, so they pass even for a bogus key. Only the pre-set `get_setting(key) is None` check detects an unregistered key. (2) I could not confirm that the /rtx/pathtracing/* keys are registered at that point. The repo's apps/ and Isaac Lab source do not define them, and they may only be registered by the RTX plugin defaults, so the None check could emit false-positive warnings. It should therefore stay warn-only and must not be turned into a raise or assert. The 'RealTimePathTracing' remark is unverified from the repo and should be dropped or treated as optional.

result.title: PointInstancer prototypes are children of the instancer: unproven whether RTX/FSD also draws them at the origin, and the 'invisible' / 'inactive' fixes would delete every rock
result.description: Answer to item 2. What is established: (a) USD itself says prototype children of a PointInstancer are pruned from raw drawing by UsdImaging and BBoxCache (see evidence), so a stock Hydra does not draw them in place. (b) Isaac Sim 5.1 + Isaac Lab 2.3 run the Fabric Scene Delegate (apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit: app.useFabricSceneDelegate = true), which is NOT UsdImaging, and I found no source that states whether FSD prunes children-of-instancer prototypes. (c) OmniGibson (a large Isaac Sim user) found that prototype prims ARE rendered in place in Omniverse, and that hiding them is not possible. Their code moves prototypes to a graveyard position with the comment 'We can't directly hide the prototype because it will also hide all the generated particles'. So the 'invisible on a Prototypes scope' fix is wrong: in Omniverse, instance visibility follows the prototype's visibility, and USD computes the child as invisible (verified with usd-core: MakeInvisible on the scope gives ComputeVisibility()=invisible for rock_0). The 'inactive scope' fix is also wrong: usd-core shows that after SetActive(False) on the Prototypes scope the prototype prims no longer exist in the composed stage (GetPrimAtPath(target).IsValid() is False), so the instancer has nothing to instance. The only USD-documented way to keep prototypes out of generic traversal is a 'class' or 'over' scope. I verified the exact authoring (below) in usd-core, but I cannot verify that FSD resolves prototypes under a non-defined prim: a community report shows FSD logging '[usdrt.hydra.fabric_scene_delegate.plugin] GeomSubset prim does not exist: .../PeopleInstancer/Prototypes/char_NN/...' when it cannot resolve prototype subtrees. Graveyarding by moving the prototype root is renderer-dependent (USD's own ComputeInstanceTransformsAtTime(IncludeProtoXform) applies the prototype root transform to every instance: I measured instance translation (5,0,-5000) for a root at z=-5000) so it can shift all rocks. Conclusion: run a 1-frame probe first, then apply the decision table in the fix.
result.evidence: OpenUSD pxr/usd/usdGeom/pointInstancer.h (copy: scratchpad/ext_ev/pointInstancer.h L214-251): 'We encourage organizing all prototypes as children of the PointInstancer prim that consumes them, and pruning "raw" processing and drawing traversals when they encounter a PointInstancer prim; this is what the UsdGeomBBoxCache and UsdImaging engines do.' ... 'to protect prototypes from all generic traversals and processing, place them under a prim that is a "class" or "over". "class" is recommended, while "over" should be used when backwards compatibility with older versions of USD is needed.' StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K OmniGibson/omnigibson/utils/physx_utils.py L195-197 (scratchpad/ext_ev/og_physx_utils.py): '# Move the prototype to the graveyard position so that it won't be visible to the agent  # We can't directly hide the prototype because it will also hide all the generated particles (if not isosurface)  prototype_prim.GetAttribute("xformOp:translate").Set(m.PROTOTYPE_GRAVEYARD_POS)'. usd-core 26.08 experiments in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/rt_review/{over_proto2.py,inactive_proto.py,over_proto.py}: (1) Mesh.Define() under an OverridePrim() scope silently turns the scope back into 'def', so SetSpecifier must come after the children are defined; (2) after SetSpecifier(Sdf.SpecifierOver): Traverse() = ['/World','/World/Rocks_0'], TraverseAll() still lists the prototypes, GetPrimAtPath(target).IsValid()=True, IsDefined()=False, ComputeInstanceTransformsAtTime still returns 2 transforms. Isaac Lab itself only notes: 'Omniverse does not support instanceable assets when using the UsdGeom.PointInstancer schema' (docs/source/refs/issues.rst:66-71); your prototypes are plain meshes, so that does not apply.
result.fix:
Step 1, probe (about 5 min, decides everything). Standalone script, run with ./isaaclab.sh -p probe.py --headless --enable_cameras:
    import argparse, os
    from isaaclab.app import AppLauncher
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); AppLauncher.add_app_launcher_args(ap); a = ap.parse_args(); a.enable_cameras = True
    app = AppLauncher(a).app
    import torch, isaaclab.sim as su
    from isaaclab.sensors import Camera, CameraCfg
    from pxr import UsdGeom, Sdf
    sim = su.SimulationContext(su.SimulationCfg(dt=1/30)); st = sim.stage
    dome = su.DomeLightCfg(intensity=1000.0); dome.func('/World/Sky', dome)
    UsdGeom.Xform.Define(st, '/World'); inst = UsdGeom.PointInstancer.Define(st, '/World/Inst')
    cube = UsdGeom.Cube.Define(st, '/World/Inst/Prototypes/cube'); cube.CreateDisplayColorAttr([(1,0,0)])
    inst.CreatePrototypesRel().SetTargets([cube.GetPath()]); inst.CreateProtoIndicesAttr([0]); inst.CreatePositionsAttr([(0,300,0)])  # the only instance is 300 m out of view
    if os.environ.get('MODE') == 'over': st.GetPrimAtPath('/World/Inst/Prototypes').SetSpecifier(Sdf.SpecifierOver)
    cam = Camera(CameraCfg(prim_path='/World/Cam', update_period=0.0, height=240, width=320, data_types=['rgb'], spawn=su.PinholeCameraPinholeCfg if False else su.PinholeCameraCfg(focal_length=18.0, horizontal_aperture=20.955, clipping_range=(0.05,1000.0)), offset=CameraCfg.OffsetCfg(pos=(-4.0,0.0,0.0), convention='world')))
    sim.reset()
    for _ in range(30): sim.step()
    cam.update(1/30); rgb = cam.data.output['rgb'][0].float()
    print('RED PIXELS AT ORIGIN:', int(((rgb[...,0]>150)&(rgb[...,1]<80)&(rgb[...,2]<80)).sum()))
  Run once as is (MODE unset) and once with MODE=over. As a control, set positions to (0,0,0) and expect red pixels in both modes.
Step 2, decision: if the default run prints 0, prototypes are NOT drawn in place under FSD: change nothing. If it prints >0 and MODE=over prints 0 and the control still shows the instance, apply in usd_scene.py after the prototype loop (L192-196), per instancer: `stage.GetPrimAtPath(f"{root}/Prototypes").SetSpecifier(Sdf.SpecifierOver)` (exactly this order: after define_mesh, because Define() resets an over ancestor to def), and in scripts/heavy_machines/test/test_usd_scene.py change meshes() to iterate self.stage.TraverseAll() so the rock prototypes stay covered by the well-formed/bound-material test. If MODE=over makes the control instance disappear, FSD cannot resolve over prototypes: keep them as def and accept the originals, which sit at the world origin (ADT front axle stop, mostly inside the ground and the tyres), or relocate them only after probing that the instance positions stay unchanged. Never use MakeInvisible() or SetActive(False) on the Prototypes scope.

verdict.reason: The finding does not hold. It is a speculative risk with no demonstrated defect, and it admits that nothing in the evidence shows FSD drawing instancer-child prototypes in place. (1) The pattern in usd_scene.py L189-196 (prototypes as children of the PointInstancer, targets set via the prototypes relationship) is the one USD recommends in pointInstancer.h, which the finding itself quotes. It is also the pattern Isaac Lab uses for VisualizationMarkers. source/isaaclab/isaaclab/markers/visualization_markers.py L67-69 and L344-358 create each prototype as a child of the instancer and add it via GetPrototypesRel().AddTarget, with no hiding, no 'over' specifier, and no graveyard move. Isaac Lab ships those markers in the viewport and in camera renders under the same FSD-enabled kit apps. If the prototypes were drawn in place at the origin, every marker user would see a stray extra marker at the origin, and the code makes no attempt to prevent that. (2) The OmniGibson graveyard evidence concerns particle systems whose prototypes are not necessarily children of the instancer. It does not show that instancer-child prototypes render in place, so it is weak support. (3) The finding's only concrete observation, that usd-core accepts a 'class' or 'over' scope, is not evidence of a runtime problem. The finding also concedes that the 'over' fix may break FSD resolution, citing the GeomSubset error report, and that its own proposed fix could shift the rocks. The proposed change would therefore add risk to code that follows the documented pattern. (4) The rest of the fix is a conditional probe with a decision table, not a corrective change. The finding gives no evidence that the unconditional state is wrong. A 1-frame probe is cheap if someone wants empirical confirmation, but it is not a reason to change usd_scene.py or test_usd_scene.py. The finding's advice never to use MakeInvisible or SetActive on the Prototypes scope is correct but moot, because the code does not do either.

result.title: Glass opacity 0.42 may be ignored by RTX: Omniverse's UsdPreviewSurface gates opacity<1 behind hidden enable_specular_transmission, which is not authored
result.description: Answer to item 1 (opacity < 1 with translucency). The Omniverse RTX UsdPreviewSurface.mdl implements the spec's 'transparent' opacityMode as a layer between diffuse and specular transmission, but only when the hidden uniform bool enable_specular_transmission is true (default false); cutout needs enable_opacity AND opacityThreshold > 0. Both flags are Omniverse-specific inputs (exported by Omniverse as 'connectability = interfaceOnly' with default 0). pbr_material() authors only the standard 'opacity'. I could not establish from public sources whether Kit's UsdPreviewSurface network translator derives enable_specular_transmission from opacity < 1 for plain pxr-authored materials, so the cab/windscreen glass (opacity 0.42 from pbr_textures._GLASS_OPACITY) might render as opaque tinted panels in both PT and RT. That is a silent look change, not a crash. If translucency does work, authoring the flag is harmless. Related details that are fine: the MDL sets thin_walled=false and ior=1.5, so each glass box is a solid slab (refraction through a 3 cm parallel slab is nearly undistorted); I verified all 77 machine meshes (incl. both glass meshes, signed volume +0.088 and +0.129) have outward winding that agrees with the authored vertex normals, so inside/outside is determined correctly. Metallic parts are forced opaque by the MDL (lerp(opacity,1,metallic)); glass has metallic=0. In RT mode, translucency additionally needs /rtx/translucency/enabled, which RenderCfg sets.
result.evidence: Reference RTX MDL (Isaac Sim 4.5.0 kit/mdl/rtx/UsdPreviewSurface.mdl, 'Revision 4'; copy at scratchpad/ext_ev/UsdPreviewSurface.mdl; the 5.1/Kit 107 file was not available, so treat as the closest primary source): 'uniform bool enable_opacity = false [[anno::hidden(), annotation_not_connectable()]]', 'uniform bool enable_specular_transmission = false [[anno::hidden(), ...]]', 'float opacity_adjusted = (!enable_specular_transmission) ? 1.0 : math::lerp(opacity, 1.0, metallic);', 'float cutout_opacity = (enable_opacity && (opacityThreshold > opacity)) ? 0.0 : 1.0;', 'bsdf mix_diff_transm = df::weighted_layer(weight: opacity_adjusted, layer: diff_bsdf, base: transm_bsdf);' and 'in material(ior: color(ior), thin_walled: false, surface: surface, backface: surface, ...)'. OpenUSD docs/spec_usdpreviewsurface.rst: opacityMode default 'transparent': 'opacity reduces the contribution of the diffuse lighting component in favor of transparency, while the specular response and emissive component remain at full weight'. Omniverse-authored materials list both flags, e.g. SICKAG/pumolink LightBarrier.usda: 'bool inputs:enable_opacity = 0 (connectability = "interfaceOnly")'.
result.fix:
In pbr_material() right after L70 add:
    if opacity < 1.0:
        # Omniverse-only gate for opacity<1 in UsdPreviewSurface.mdl; leave enable_opacity unauthored (that is the cutout path and needs opacityThreshold>0)
        pbr.CreateInput('enable_specular_transmission', Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Bool).Set(True)
Then render one test frame of the ADT cab and confirm the dark interior or body shell is visible through the windows (with the flag on, 58 percent of the light is transmitted). Add `assert surf.GetInput('enable_specular_transmission').Get()` for opacity<1 materials to test_usd_scene.py. If the cab interior is just an opaque body shell behind the glass, consider lowering transmission (raise opacity to about 0.6) so the windows read as tinted glass over a dark interior rather than see-through to the body panel.

verdict.reason: The finding is unproven and its own text says so. The MDL source does gate the transmission mix on a hidden enable_specular_transmission flag (UsdPreviewSurface.mdl in the scratchpad: line 365 default false, line 427 opacity_adjusted = !enable_specular_transmission ? 1.0 : lerp(...)). So an authored opacity alone has no effect in that file as written. But that file is from Isaac Sim 4.5, not 5.1, and nothing in the repo or Isaac Lab source shows how Kit's UsdPreviewSurface network translator sets these hidden flags. A grep of the repo found no use of enable_specular_transmission or enable_opacity. The finding admits it 'could not establish' whether the translator derives the flag from opacity < 1. I also have no precisely citable Omniverse documentation showing that plain pxr-authored UsdPreviewSurface opacity < 1 is ignored by RTX. From general knowledge, Omniverse and Isaac Sim do generally render pxr-authored UsdPreviewSurface opacity < 1 as translucent, because Kit's translator handles it. I can't cite a source for that, though. The failure mode is therefore speculation. I could not run Isaac Sim here to settle it, and usd-core cannot show RTX behaviour. Authoring the flag would probably do no harm, but that is a speculative hardening step, not a demonstrated defect.

result.title: Exposure chain is not pinned: auto-exposure/tonemapper can change per frame, and camera_look re-tonemaps on top of whatever RTX applied
result.description: Answer to item 5. Lights: DistantLight 3000 and DomeLight 1000 with kloofendal_43d_clear_puresky_4k.hdr are in the normal Isaac Lab range (DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0) is used throughout the Isaac Lab tests; DomeLightCfg(intensity=750) with the same HDR in the locomotion task), so they are not blown out by construction. Back-of-envelope using the reference MDL (an emissive of 1.0 is scaled by PI*1133.6 'such that its value is the same as the exposed pixel value with our default camera exposure settings'): a white surface at about 1.1e3 nits maps to pixel 1.0, so sun-lit mid-grey sand (albedo 0.3-0.6) lands around 0.2-0.5 linear and white paint around 0.7-0.8, the sky about 0.2-0.5; sun:sky illuminance is only roughly 2:1, so shadows will be soft and filled (assumes DistantLight intensity is irradiance-like and a mean HDR value of about 0.4; order of magnitude only). The real risk is the unpinned post chain: (1) /rtx/post/histogram/enabled (auto exposure) is on in many Omniverse apps (USD Composer scenes write it explicitly) and community Isaac Sim users report that it makes brightness follow scene content, so the exposure would drift as the sky/ground ratio changes during the clip and in the 40 warm-up frames; (2) /rtx/post/tonemap/op is set by the Kit build, not by Isaac Lab (no tonemap key in apps/*.kit or rendering_modes), and camera_look then decodes sRGB and applies its own highlight shoulder plus S-curve, so a filmic RTX operator gives a double tone curve (extra contrast and saturation, crushed shadows); (3) /rtx/sceneDb/ambientLightIntensity = 1.0 is set by every Isaac Lab preset (and Composer PT scenes zero rtx:sceneDb:ambientLightColor), a small non-physical fill. I could not read the Kit 107 defaults (docs hosts blocked), so the correct fix is to pin and log rather than to guess.
result.evidence: Settings exist and are pinned in Isaac Sim user code: '/rtx/post/histogram/enabled' False with comment 'no auto-exposure' and '/rtx/post/tonemap/op' 1 with comment 'linear, no filmic shoulder' (YenCho/ddonggae simulation/README.md L259-263: 'With auto-exposure on, a lighting sweep converges on nothing'); '/rtx/post/tonemap/filmIso', 'cameraShutter', 'fNumber', 'whitepoint', 'exposureTime', 'enableSrgbToGamma', 'dither' appear in CanelE452/Korea-Railroad-project gen_replicator_data.py, ukkhnn/PAC2026 run_isaac_welding_scene.py, jeffrey-ke/isaac_datagen scene.py, RobotEurekaLab/Hooke isaac_worker.py. The op enum numbering is inconsistent between these sources (1 linear per ddonggae, 2 in 3dgrut nurec export, 4 labelled 'Reinhard' in Korea-Railroad, 6 in OpenRAL), so log the value instead of trusting a number. Isaac Lab: DistantLightCfg(intensity=3000.0, color=(0.75,0.75,0.75)) in source/isaaclab/test/scene/check_interactive_scene.py:74; DomeLightCfg(intensity=750.0, texture_file=.../kloofendal_43d_clear_puresky_4k.hdr) in isaaclab_tasks locomotion/velocity/velocity_env_cfg.py:80. camera_look.py header: 'sRGB decode (x exposure x white balance) -> ... -> highlight shoulder + S-curve (one LUT)'.
result.fix:
After the PT/RTX block (render_scenario.py ~L148) add:
    for k in ('/rtx/post/histogram/enabled','/rtx/post/tonemap/op','/rtx/post/tonemap/filmIso','/rtx/post/tonemap/cameraShutter','/rtx/post/tonemap/fNumber','/rtx/post/tonemap/whitepoint'):
        print(f'[scenario] {k} = {sim.get_setting(k)!r}', flush=True)
    sim.set_setting('/rtx/post/histogram/enabled', False)     # fixed exposure for a video
and decide the tone curve once: either keep RTX filmic and set camera_look to a neutral shoulder, or set /rtx/post/tonemap/op to the linear operator (verify the enum from the logged default and ddonggae's 1) and keep camera_look's shoulder; do not leave both active unintentionally. Calibrate with a 5-line check after warm-up: lum = 0.2126*r+0.7152*g+0.0722*b on the raw frame; print p50, p99 and the fraction of pixels >= 250 for the front camera at t=0 and t=8.5 s; target p99 < 245 and clipped fraction < 1 percent. Adjust with the light's exposure (DistantLightCfg(exposure=...), a log2 multiplier) rather than intensity, and if shadows look too flat, raise sun_intensity or lower sky_intensity together with a negative exposure to keep the sunlit highlights below clipping. Consider also sim.set_setting('/rtx/sceneDb/ambientLightColor', (0.0,0.0,0.0)) for the PT path (verify with get_setting that it exists).

verdict.reason: The repo does not support the claim that exposure drifts or that the tone curve is doubled. In apps/ and source/isaaclab/isaaclab, grep finds no tonemap, histogram or auto-exposure keys, so nothing there sets or implies either behaviour. render_scenario.py only sets PT keys (rendermode, spp, totalSpp, optixDenoiser, maxBounces). The finding's own text says the Kit 107 defaults could not be read. Its claims that auto-exposure is on by default and that the RTX operator is filmic are inferred from other projects' user code and from Composer scenes that write the key explicitly. That user code shows the settings exist and can be pinned; it does not show the Isaac Sim default is on or filmic. The enum numbers it cites disagree across those sources, so they cannot be trusted. The lighting numbers are order-of-magnitude estimates that rest on assumptions. camera_look.py being a deliberate downstream grade does not make it a double-tonemap bug without knowing the RTX operator, which is not demonstrated. At most this is an unverified suggestion to log the settings and pin them for reproducibility. It is not a demonstrated runtime defect.

result.title: assets_loading() does not cover texture mip streaming or the remote dome HDR; first recorded frames can be blurry or have a black sky
result.description: SimulationManager.assets_loading() returns 'not _assets_loaded', and that flag is only toggled by the stage events ASSETS_LOADING / ASSETS_LOADED. It tells you the initial asset/material load is done, not that RTX texture streaming has refined the mips of the 7800x3900 and 6720x2760 terrain maps (streaming is on in Isaac Sim configurations; Isaac Lab's XR kits switch it off as an optimisation). Your warm-up is 40 frames x 4 renders; that is probably enough, but nothing verifies it. Separately, the sky HDR is a remote S3 URL that RTX fetches during the run: check_file_path() only tells you the file existed at build time (it is a synchronous omni.client.stat that blocks until the client timeout when offline, then returns 0 and you fall back, so no crash). If the transfer fails or stalls later, the dome stays black or unlit and every frame is recorded without any error. Isaac Lab documents the related symptom: 'the first few frames may be blank ... it needs a few steps to load the material textures properly and fill up the render targets'.
result.evidence: Isaac Sim simulation_manager.py L595-613 and L1393-1408 (scratchpad/ext_ev/ss_simmgr.py): _assets_loading sets _assets_loaded=False and _assets_loaded sets True on the ASSETS_LOADING / ASSETS_LOADED stage events; 'assets_loading ... Check if the textures of the assets are being loaded.' returns 'not cls._assets_loaded'. Isaac Sim extension test args: '--/rtx-transient/resourcemanager/enableTextureStreaming=1' (isaac-sim/IsaacSim isaacsim.core.api/config/extension.toml); Isaac Lab apps/isaaclab.python.xr.openxr.kit: "# xr optimizations ... 'rtx-transient'.resourcemanager.enableTextureStreaming = false". Isaac Lab docs/source/refs/issues.rst:48-63 ('Blank initial frames from the camera'). source/isaaclab/isaaclab/utils/assets.py:43-62 (check_file_path returns 0/1/2, omni.client.stat for URLs).
result.fix: 1) Disable streaming for this offline renderer (key confirmed in Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab configs; it is an rtx-transient key, so pass it at launch rather than at runtime): ./isaaclab.sh -p scripts/heavy_machines/scenarios/render_scenario.py --scenario adt_approach_hex --headless --kit_args "--/rtx-transient/resourcemanager/enableTextureStreaming=0"   (GPU cost: all terrain mips resident, about 0.6-1 GB). 2) Cache the HDR locally so no network is needed during rendering: in build_lights() use `from isaaclab.utils.assets import retrieve_file_path; hdr_local = retrieve_file_path(hdr, download_dir=os.path.join(out,'textures'), force_download=False)` and pass texture_file=hdr_local (wrap in try/except and fall back to the sky colour). 3) Add a settle check after the assets loop: render the static t=0 state until two consecutive frames agree, i.e. loop up to 600 times { advance() without apply_state(); mean|rgb_k - rgb_{k-1}| < 0.3 for 3 consecutive iterations }; with PT stopped at totalSpp, any remaining difference means textures or the dome are still changing.

verdict.reason:
The finding is speculation, and its own text concedes the warm-up is "probably enough". Most of its factual premises check out. Nothing in the repo or in documented Omniverse behaviour shows that frames are actually recorded blurry or with a black sky.

What is accurate:
- The runner warms up for 40 frames of `advance()` (each a `sim.step` plus `subframes-1` renders), then loops on `SimulationManager.assets_loading()` for up to 3000 iterations (render_scenario.py L190-199).
- `apps/isaaclab.python.headless.kit:69` sets `'rtx-transient'.resourcemanager.enableTextureStreaming = true`.
- Only the XR kits turn streaming off, per the finding (`apps/isaaclab.python.xr.openxr.kit:37` and `apps/isaaclab.python.xr.openxr.headless.kit:27`).
- `docs/source/refs/issues.rst:48-63` documents blank first frames, and its suggested workaround is 12 `sim.render()` steps. The existing 40 warm-up frames plus the `assets_loading()` loop already go well beyond that.
- `check_file_path` and `retrieve_file_path` exist in `assets.py`, as described.

Why it still does not hold:
- Nothing shows the 40-frame warm-up plus the `assets_loading()` loop is insufficient for the 7800x3900 and 6720x2760 maps. The claim that mips might not be refined is a hypothetical. I found no repo evidence, and no precisely citable Omniverse documentation, that these maps stay blurry after this many renders. RTX streaming prioritises the mips visible in the current view, and this loop renders that view repeatedly.
- The black-sky claim depends on a remote transfer failing silently mid-run. That is also hypothetical. The code already falls back to a plain sky colour when the HDR is unreachable, and there is a `--no_sky_hdr` flag for offline runs.
- The finding's own text says a build-time `check_file_path` failure falls back to the sky colour with no crash. That leaves only a hypothetical later stall.
- The proposed fixes are unverified and have costs:
  - The `--kit_args` route for the rtx-transient key appends the arguments to `sys.argv` (app_launcher.py L780-786). Whether the key takes effect that way is unproven.
  - A settle loop of up to 600 iterations with a mean-difference threshold of 0.3 is arbitrary and untested. The finding gives no validated reason it would converge, and it slows every run.
  - Caching the HDR locally is only a robustness nicety, not a demonstrated bug fix.

This is a speculative hardening suggestion, not a verified defect, so the default of holds=false stands. If anything, the doc-supported mitigation is to raise `--warmup`, which already exists as an argument.

result.title: Per-frame restart of PT with a non-temporal denoiser can shimmer; fireflies from sun-through-glass caustics
result.description: Every video frame restarts accumulation (by design) at 128 spp and is denoised independently by the OptiX denoiser, so fine terrain detail and the sun/glass caustic noise can flicker slightly from frame to frame. The keys below exist in NVIDIA's own tooling. This is a quality tuning item, not a defect. The glass boxes use a non-thin-walled IOR 1.5 transmission with a distant light: NEE cannot connect through refraction, so bright fireflies in the shadow of cab glass are likely at low spp.
result.evidence: NVIDIA/paidf-simulation scripts/sdg/standalone/common.py lists '/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/enabled', '/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/temporalMode/enabled', '/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/blendFactor', '/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/AOV', '/rtx/pathtracing/fireflyFilter/enabled', '/rtx/pathtracing/aa/op', '/rtx/pathtracing/aa/filterRadius'; YCJ0815/3D-Diffusion-Policy comment '# 0 = denoised output; 1 = original noisy radiance' for blendFactor. Other users use '/rtx/pathtracing/maxSpecularAndTransmissionBounces' (VoMP replicator_renderer.py: 8) for glass.
result.fix: Optional A/B on 30 frames: (a) '/rtx/pathtracing/optixDenoiser/temporalMode/enabled' True (less shimmer, check for ghosting on the moving truck at 3 m/s); (b) '/rtx/pathtracing/fireflyFilter/enabled' True; (c) '/rtx/pathtracing/maxSpecularAndTransmissionBounces' 8 for the slab glass; (d) raise --spp 32 --subframes 4 to --spp 32 --subframes 8 if render time allows. Run each key through the get_setting() presence check from the set_setting finding.

verdict.reason: The finding is speculative tuning advice, and the part about glass is not supported by the repo. (1) I found no Isaac Lab source or app preset in the repo that uses any of the proposed keys. Grepping source/ and apps/ for optixDenoiser, fireflyFilter, temporalMode and maxSpecularAndTransmissionBounces returned nothing. The only pathtracing key in source/ is /rtx/pathtracing/maxSamplesPerLaunch, in a test. The keys are backed only by third-party repos the finding cites, and I did not verify those. The finding itself says the change is optional and only "likely" to help. (2) The glass premise is not shown in the code. usd_scene.py:63-70 builds every material, glass included, as a UsdPreviewSurface with an opacity input. It has no OmniGlass, no explicit IOR, no transmission and no thin_walled setting. The machine boxes use mat="glass" with collision=False in mini_excavator.py:315 and hydraulic_excavator.py:435. Whether RTX path tracing treats a UsdPreviewSurface with opacity < 1 as refractive IOR 1.5 transmission or as simple alpha transparency is not shown. So the claim that NEE cannot connect through refraction and gives sun-through-glass caustic fireflies is unproven for this scene. Solid cab glass slabs of thickness 0.02-0.03 m could just as well render as ordinary alpha-translucent surfaces with no caustic path. (3) The shimmer claim is also not demonstrated. Each frame does sim.step plus subframes-1 extra render calls with spp samples each, and totalSpp is set to spp*subframes (render_scenario.py:140-141), so each frame is an independent 128-spp accumulation. That per-frame independence is by design, and whether it visibly shimmers is an empirical question I cannot test here. The finding reports no measurement. (4) The suggested temporalMode would be risky for this scene. The truck and camera move every frame, and the key is not in the repo's Isaac Lab source, so a temporal denoiser could ghost. It is an A/B experiment, not a defect fix. Also, the existing loop around line 142 already wraps each set_setting in try/except, so an unknown key only prints a message, but there is no get_setting() presence check in the code.

result.title: Texture/mesh limits are fine, but the CPU bake is single-threaded and takes about 14 minutes on 4 cores before the first frame, with Kit not pumped
result.description: Answer to item 6. Sizes from the real scenario: near strip 56x23 m = albedo 2688x1104 (3.0 Mpx), relief maps 120 px/m = 6720x2760 (18.5 Mpx); local 130x65 m = albedo 3120x1560 (4.9 Mpx), relief 60 px/m = 7800x3900 (30.4 Mpx); far albedo 1800x1800 (3.2 Mpx). detail_px_per_m() already caps at 16384 per side and 40 Mpx, and the largest side used is 7800, so no hard limit is reached; total about 109 Mpx of PNG, roughly 0.6 GB of GPU texture memory even if single-channel maps are expanded to RGBA8 with mips. Geometry (measured): terrain 2,990,328 triangles = near 114,138 + local 636,684 + far 2,239,506. The far part is 75 percent of the triangles and 1.12 M vertices because the tensor-product graded grid carries the fine local row/column spacing out to +-900 m, which creates thin slivers; it is wasteful but not a limit. Rocks: 11,102 instances (160 boulders + 10,942 gravel, not 5k) over 3 instancers x 8 prototypes (five of 5120 tris, three of 320), about 4.3 M instanced triangles, which RTX instances through the TLAS cheaply. Machine twins: ADT 58,044 + HEX 135,696 = 193,740 triangles, 77 meshes. Bake times measured on this 4-core box with the real code (single thread): bake_albedo about 43 s/Mpx (0.19 Mpx 7.2 s, 0.74 Mpx 32 s; far 1800x1800 225 s), so near about 130 s, local about 213 s, far 225 s; terrain_detail_maps about 0.65 Mpx/s (near about 28 s, local about 47 s); terrain_detail_cavity about 1.4 s/Mpx; split_terrain_meshes 122 s; machine_textures 1024: 3.0 s (body) / 0.9 s (glass) x about 19 sets; scatter 3 s. Total about 14 min, peak RSS 1.1 GB. A fast workstation core is perhaps 2x faster: 6-9 min. Everything runs inside the Kit process before sim.reset(), so Kit's main loop is not pumped for that time: harmless headless, 'Not Responding' in the GUI.

HEX visual tris 135696'. pbr_textures.py:1081-1093 (max_pixels 40e6, 16384 per side).
result.fix: 1) Cache the bakes: key the three terrain PNGs (and the far PNG) by a hash of (scenario name, rects, ppm values, seeds, boulders, gravel_per_m2, a code version string) and skip bake_albedo / terrain_detail_* / contact_map when the files and a marker exist; this turns re-runs into seconds. 2) Parallelise the independent jobs with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4): near albedo, local albedo, far albedo and split_terrain_meshes are independent (wall time becomes about the slowest job, 225 s, instead of about 690 s). 3) Print a progress line per job (they already use log()). 4) Optional: build the far mesh as a separate coarse grid (cap 6-8 m outside local_rect) to cut about 2 M slivers; Image.save(..., compress_level=1) for the big PNGs saves tens of seconds.

verdict.reason: Supported as a low-severity performance improvement. The bake runs in-process: render_scenario.py imports build_scene from usd_scene.py after AppLauncher starts Kit (lines 53-69), and sim.reset() is at line 166. _terrain_material (usd_scene.py ~L134-145) calls bake_albedo, terrain_detail_cavity, contact_map and terrain_detail_maps synchronously. A grep for cache, exists(), ProcessPool and hash in usd_scene.py and render_scenario.py found no caching or parallelism, so every run re-bakes. Kit's main loop is not pumped during the bake, which is harmless headless and gives 'Not Responding' in the GUI. The per-stage timings come from the measurement scripts in rt_review/ and are plausible, but I did not re-run them. Caching is clearly sound. The proposed ProcessPoolExecutor inside the Kit process is risky: fork from a multithreaded, CUDA-initialised Kit process, or spawn using Kit's python and re-importing the module, can hang or misbehave. Parallelism should run outside Kit or use a spawn context with top-level picklable functions. Reasonable hard limits (texture sizes, mesh counts) are not hit, so this is an improvement, not a bug.
verdict.corrected_fix: 1) Cache the bakes: key each terrain PNG set (near, local, far) by a hash of (scenario name, rects, ppm values, seeds, boulders, gravel_per_m2, a code version string). Skip bake_albedo, terrain_detail_* and contact_map when the files and a marker file exist, so re-runs take seconds. 2) Do not use fork or a ProcessPoolExecutor inside the Kit process. Either run the bakes in a pre-step before AppLauncher is created, for example a separate 'python -m heavy_machines.scenarios.usd_scene --bake' subprocess run from render_scenario.py (subprocess is already imported), or use ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4, mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context('spawn')) with top-level picklable worker functions that import only numpy and PIL. The near albedo, local albedo, far albedo and split_terrain_meshes jobs are independent, so wall time drops to roughly the slowest job (about 225 s) instead of about 690 s. 3) Log one progress line per job through the existing log(). 4) Optional: use compress_level=1 for the big PNGs, and build the far mesh as a coarse separate grid to remove about 2 M sliver triangles. Document that the GUI shows 'Not Responding' during the bake, or run the bake as a pre-step so Kit is not started until it finishes.

result.title: VERIFIED OK: the UsdPreviewSurface network as authored is supported by Omniverse RTX (items: scale/bias normal map, r channel, raw/sRGB, clamp/repeat, absolute paths, clearcoat)
result.description: No change required except the opacity gate in the separate finding. Checked against the Omniverse reference MDL and the OpenUSD spec. (1) UsdUVTexture scale/bias: Omniverse computes 'float4 f = float4(tint.x, tint.y, tint.z, texRet.mono) * scale + bias', and the monolithic variant carries scale, bias, wrapS/T, sourceColorSpace and a channel selector per input, so the normal map (scale (2,2,2,1), bias (-1,-1,-1,0), sourceColorSpace raw) is exactly the spec's 8-bit recipe. (2) The 'r' output of a single-channel (mode L) roughness PNG is defined by the spec: 'If a single-channel texture is fed into a UsdUVTexture, the r, g, and b components of the rgb output will repeat the channel's value'. (3) The normal input becomes shading_normal = normalize(tangent_u*n.x + tangent_v*n.y + normal*n.z) using texture coordinate 0 ('st'); your maps are OpenGL (+Y = +v) tangent space and I verified in code that UV u follows +x (corr 1.0) and v follows +y (corr 1.0), with image row 0 = y1 = v=1, which is the USD/MDL lower-left-origin convention. (4) wrapS/T tokens 'clamp' and 'repeat' are in the spec list (black, clamp, repeat, mirror, useMetadata). Clamp is the right choice for the terrain: the Near mesh UVs reach u 0.00076..0.9995 and v 0.0028..1.0014, slightly outside [0,1]. (5) Absolute PNG paths as Asset inputs are fine; the files are written before they are referenced. (6) Clearcoat is implemented as df::custom_curve_layer(weight: clearcoat, layer: GGX(clearcoatRoughness^2)), but every current material authors clearcoat 0 (TextureSet.clearcoat is never set above 0), so it is unexercised. (7) Per the spec, 'varname' is typed string and the code authors Token; Omniverse reads both in practice, and switching to Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String (L77) is the spec-exact form if you want zero doubt. Caveat: 'sourceColorSpace' is marked anno::unused() in the MDL, i.e. it is honoured by the renderer's texture loader, not by the shader, so it cannot be proven offline: if the albedo looks washed out or the terrain relief looks flat in the first test render, that is the place to look.
result.evidence: scratchpad/ext_ev/UsdPreviewSurface.mdl (Isaac Sim 4.5.0 kit/mdl/rtx, Revision 4) UsdUVTexture: 'float4 f = float4(tint.x, tint.y, tint.z, texRet.mono) * scale + bias;' and 'uniform string sourceColorSpace = "auto" [[ anno::unused() ]]'; shading_normal expression: 'math::normalize(uvw.tangent_u * normal.x + uvw.tangent_v * normal.y + state::normal() * normal.z)' with 'Always use st idx 0, for normal mapping'. UsdPreviewSurfaceMonolithic.mdl: 'default to state::texture_coordinate(0) which is "st" or "st0"' and per-input '*_scale', '*_bias', '*_channel', '*_wrapS', '*_sourceColorSpace'. OpenUSD docs/spec_usdpreviewsurface.rst: 'If the texture has 8 bits per component, then scale and bias must be adjusted to be (2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 1.0) and (-1, -1, -1, 0) ... the sourceColorSpace must also be set to "raw"'; wrapS options 'black, clamp, repeat, mirror, useMetadata'; 'string inputs:varname'. Local check: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/rt_review/winding2.py printed 'uv u increases with +x? 1.0  v increases with +y? 0.9999999999999981' and 'terrain faces with downward winding normal: 0.0'.
result.fix: None required. Optional hardening: line 77, `st.CreateInput('varname', Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set('st')` (spec type). Keep clamp for all three terrain materials.

verdict.reason: Holds as a no-defect finding. I checked the cited Omniverse MDL (scratchpad/ext_ev/UsdPreviewSurface.mdl) and the authoring code in usd_scene.py. MDL line 298 computes 'float4 f = float4(tint.x, tint.y, tint.z, texRet.mono) * scale + bias', so the normal map's scale (2,2,2,1) and bias (-1,-1,-1,0) with sourceColorSpace raw match the OpenUSD 8-bit normal-map recipe. Line 445 builds the shading normal as tangent_u*normal.x + tangent_v*normal.y + state::normal()*normal.z. In the MDL, sourceColorSpace is declared with anno::unused() (lines 281-283), so it is applied by the texture loader and not by the shader. As the finding says, that cannot be proven offline. The authored network is as the finding describes. It has a UsdPrimvarReader_float2 'st' reader feeding UsdUVTexture inputs, wrap tokens clamp or repeat, and an r output for the roughness map. The albedo is read as sRGB and the normal and roughness maps as raw. In the MDL, the primvar-reader varname is a uniform string, and the UsdPreviewSurface network is the standard Omniverse path. Authoring varname as Token is a widely used Omniverse convention. Switching to String is only optional spec-exactness hardening. I did not independently re-run the UV and winding checks, and the clearcoat and Isaac Sim 5.1 runtime behaviour are unverified here. The finding's own caveat covers sourceColorSpace.

result.title: VERIFIED OK: camera depth type and sky value, same-frame pose, imports, check_file_path and os._exit behave as intended
result.description: Item 4: distance_to_camera has shape (N,H,W,1) float32 (docs and tests), so data['distance_to_camera'][0, ..., 0] at L228 is the (H,W) array camera_look expects. Pixels with no hit (the DomeLight sky) and anything beyond clipping_range[1] are +inf with depth_clipping_behavior='none' (Camera forces values above clipping_range[1] to torch.inf), and camera_look already treats inf/NaN/0/>=1e5 as sky. The pinhole values are written 1:1 to USD (spawn_camera does no cm-to-mm conversion), so focal_length=10, horizontal_aperture=20.955 give a 93.3 degree HFOV and the rig comment 'mm' is right even though the Isaac Lab docstring says cm. set_world_poses(convention='world') before sim.step gives that pose's image in the same frame: it writes omni:fabric:worldMatrix, calls update_world_xforms() and mirrors to USD, and apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit sets omni.replicator.asyncRendering=false, app.renderer.waitIdle, app.hydraEngine.waitIdle and 'app.updateOrder.checkForHydraRenderComplete = 1000  # Avoids frame offset issue'. The Isaac Lab 'stale values' note applies to reading before stepping; you read after advance(). The machine link transforms are USD-authored (op.Set) rather than Fabric-written; they are tracked into Fabric by the same update, which cannot be verified offline, so keep a cheap guard (below). Item 7: `from isaacsim.core.simulation_manager import SimulationManager` after AppLauncher is exactly what Isaac Lab itself does (simulation_context.py:29, direct_rl_env.py:25) and assets_loading() is used the same way in direct_rl_env.py:327. check_file_path returns 0/1/2, so `!= 0` is correct. os._exit is safe here: every print on the build/record path is flush=True or goes through the flushing log lambda, PIL closes files in save(), ffmpeg is waited on with subprocess.run, and the exit code encodes success. Cost note: with --cameras unset both cameras are rendered on every app.update (2x PT cost); use --cameras front for tests.
result.evidence: source/isaaclab/docs/source/overview/core-concepts/sensors/camera.rst:94 ('distance_to_camera ... (B, H, W, 1) and has type torch.float32'); camera.py:525-533 and 655-663; camera_cfg.py:57-63 ('none: No clipping is applied. Values will be returned as inf.'); sensors/spawners sensors.py:136-143 (prim.GetAttribute(prim_prop_name).Set(param_value)); xform_prim_view.py:699-766 (_set_world_poses_fabric); apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit lines for asyncRendering/waitIdle/checkForHydraRenderComplete; docs/source/refs/issues.rst:8-31. Numerics: scripts/.../camera_look.py:462 'self.sky = ~((depth > 0.0) & (depth < SKY_DEPTH_M))'.
result.fix: None required. Cheap runtime guard worth adding after the first recorded frame and after the last: assert the raw front-camera frames at k=0 and k=n_frames-1 differ (mean abs diff > 1.0), which catches machines stuck at their initial pose if USD-authored transforms were ever not picked up by Fabric.

verdict.reason:
I checked the main claims against the repo source. I could not run Isaac, so the Fabric and same-frame behaviour rests on source and kit-file evidence plus documented Omniverse behaviour, not on a runtime test.

- **Depth values:** camera.py:525-533 (the replicator path) and 655-663 (the other path) set distance_to_camera values above clipping_range[1] to torch.inf. The clip-behaviour block that follows only changes inf values when depth_clipping_behavior != "none", and render_scenario.py leaves the default "none", so inf is kept. camera_look.py:462 computes `sky = ~((depth > 0) & (depth < SKY_DEPTH_M))`, which treats inf, NaN, 0 and very large values as sky. The slice `data["distance_to_camera"][0, ..., 0]` (render_scenario.py:228) gives (H, W) from the (B, H, W, 1) output.
- **Pinhole values:** spawn_camera (sensors.py:136-143) does `prim.GetAttribute(camelCase(name)).Set(param_value)` with no unit conversion. render_scenario.py:161-162 passes rig.focal_length and rig.horizontal_aperture straight through. The horizontal FOV is 2·atan(20.955 / (2·10)) = 93.3°. It depends only on the ratio, so the cm-versus-mm docstring wording does not change the result.
- **Same-frame pose:** `apply_state` sets the pose before `sim.step(render=True)`, and the data is read after `advance()`. apps/isaaclab.python.headless.rendering.kit sets asyncRendering=false (line 79), checkForHydraRenderComplete=1000 (line 82), app.renderer.waitIdle=true (line 83) and app.hydraEngine.waitIdle=true (line 84). Together these make the render synchronous, so there is no frame offset.
- **Machine links:** the machine link transforms are written with USD op.Set rather than through Fabric. Whether Fabric picks them up cannot be shown offline. The finding says so, and the proposed guard covers that gap.

I did not re-check the item 7 claims (the SimulationManager import, check_file_path return codes and os._exit safety). I also did not check the print flush=True claim in detail, the ffmpeg subprocess handling or the 2x path-tracing cost note.

The finding is rated an improvement with no required change, which is consistent with the evidence. The optional guard of comparing the raw front-camera frames at k=0 and k=n_frames-1 (mean abs diff > 1.0) is cheap and reasonable. It is a sanity check only, and it would false-fail on a scenario where the camera sees little change between the first and last frame.
verdict.corrected_fix: None required. Optional guard: when --save_raw is on, or by keeping the first and last raw front frames in memory, assert np.abs(first.astype(float) - last.astype(float)).mean() > 1.0 after recording, and warn (not abort) if it fails.
